Definition: from ἕρκος (a fence; perhaps akin to G3725); a limit, i.e. (sacred) restraint (specially, an oath):--oath.
BiblicalUsage: hórkos — oath. That is the whole of it, and it is enough: 10 occurrences, and in Matthew, Mark, Luke, and Acts the meaning never wavers. I keep coming back to the simple reading because the simple reading is the true one.
TheologicalSignificance: What hórkos tells me is that God keeps His oaths, and He expects His people to keep theirs. I hold that the simple reading is the true one, and I will not trade it for a clever one.
RelatedEvents: The Sermon on the Mount; The Death of John the Baptist; The Birth of John the Baptist
